items.title: Patriotism & Sacrifice: Preserving American Liberty - The Cougar Chronicle
items.summary: # A Land Consecrated by Sacrifice. While many are taking time to reflect on America’s exceptional achievements, I would like to take a moment to touch on the sacrifices that both forged and preserved this promised land. As the Savior put it, “no man hath greater love than this, that a man layeth down his life for his friends.” Many of those who chiseled the foundations of this nation gave that last measure of full devotion. That caliber of sacrifice is at the heart of genuine patriotism. ​America, a land consecrated by sacrifice, is the birthplace of liberty. With an iron grip, those brave soldiers continued to fight for a cause they knew to be just, inspired, and noble. In the spirit of 1776, may we be “well aware of the Toil and Blood and Treasure, that it will cost us to maintain this Declaration,” that we may see “the Rays of ravishing Light and Glory” and secure the blessings of liberty for our posterity.

items.title: Buried, Filmed, Denied - The Times of Israel
items.summary: **Buried, Filmed, Denied:** ***Jedwabne of 10 July 1941,  October 7, and the Assault on Historical Truth***. *The Jedwabne massacre, of 10 July 1941, of its local Jewish community by a cohort of non-Jewish Polish neighbors entered public memory and history writing in Poland only after almost sixty years of silence. The Hamas massacre, of October 7, 2023, of Israelis at the Nova Festival and in local kibbutzim in southern Israel, accompanied by the abduction of 251 Jewish and non-Jewish individuals including, elderly, babies and toddlers, was filmed in real time by its perpetrators, victims, and survivors. For me, as a historian of the Holocaust and its memorialization and East European Jews, July 2026 has been an especially revealing month. On 10 July, the eighty-fifth anniversary of the massacre of the Jews of Jedwabne was marked in Jedwabne, north-eastern Poland. What does the massacre of the Jews of Jedwabne on 10 July 1941 have in common with the Hamas-organized and executed massacre in southern Israel on 7 October 2023?

items.title: How the Missouri State Fair is celebrating America - Farm Progress
items.summary: # How the Missouri State Fair is celebrating America. The nation’s 250th birthday will be marked with patriotic themes throughout all fair exhibits, including livestock shows and agriculture displays. The Missouri State Fair has several events for the next generation of agriculture leaders, from livestock shows to patriotic decorating contests. Celebrating 250 years of the United States of America will be at the forefront this year at the Missouri State Fair. Fair attendees will feel the patriotic theme throughout nearly all aspects of the fair, from new events to livestock shows to even the theme of Show-Me Stars & Stripes. “We hope that our farmers really enjoy the way we showcase agriculture and what their industry brings to our state,” said Jason Moore, director of the Missouri State Fair. ## 250 years of Missouri livestock. Contests with a patriotic flair will bring fun to livestock exhibitors. Moore said the fair will be a place for Missouri farmers to celebrate.
